title: factory_core is the generic, founder-owned software-factory core
content: factory_core is Jeremy McEntire's own proprietary IP (LICENSE = proprietary; PROVENANCE.md asserts separate, independent shippability). It is generic by construction: it imports nothing target-specific. Every per-target input (repo coordinates, working-agreement docs, compliance rules, role bindings, IdP config) is DATA loaded at runtime through the adapter seams in factory_core/adapters.py, never a code dependency. The dependency arrow points consumer -> factory, never the reverse.

title: No target code in factory_core (enforced by check_core_purity)
content: factory_core/ must import only stdlib + the package itself + an allowlisted third-party set (currently jsonschema); it must contain no un-baselined target-specific token in identifiers/strings; and pyproject.toml must list no target pack as a dependency. scripts/check_core_purity.py enforces all three, fail-closed, wired into make ship. Deleting every target pack must leave the core importable, testable, and green (the portability proof in tests/test_portability.py). Trigger: any change under factory_core/. Action: block on any purity finding.

title: The evidence ledger: content-addressed, hash-chained, SoD-enforcing (factory_core/manifest.py)
content: factory_core/manifest.py is a stdlib-only, append-only ledger of lifecycle transitions. Each entry is content-addressed (SHA-256 of its canonical body) and chained to the prior entry's address (prev_hash), so tampering with any entry breaks the chain at the next link. Every append is fail-closed on segregation of duties: implementer, verifier, and approver must be three distinct identities; any two-role overlap is refused (SegregationError). An optional SegregationPolicy adds alias-canonicalization and approver-is-human resolution. Generalized from the origin target's proven single-manifest ledger pattern (a transferability review flagged that file as stdlib-only, domain-agnostic, copy-as-is); this version adds the append-only hash-chain and strips all domain specifics.

title: Phase 0 scope: core skeleton + purity guard, proven against a synthetic empty target
content: Phase 0 delivers the four core modules (manifest ledger, TargetManifest loader, five adapter Protocol seams, role/capability schema), the executable purity guard + baseline, a synthetic empty target fixture, and a full pytest suite including the portability proof. It is a real, tested foundation, NOT a running portal: the orchestration engine, PRD/spec authoring loops, RBAC/SSO, build/demo, and affinity write-back are later phases per the Factory Portal PRD v2. Open item carried forward: manifest signing / out-of-repo key anchoring (OQ17) is wired as a fail-closed seam (verify_signature + require_signature on the loader) but full PKI/rotation/revocation is deferred.

title: Factory requires ratified Testing Plan Proposal before implementation
content: Factory capability flow now requires a signed Testing Plan Proposal after Product Spec and Eng Spec approval and before implementation. The plan is a derived projection of the signed specs, not a third oracle; conflicts require source spec amendment and plan regeneration. Each row enumerates trace id, suite or type, fixture or data source, environment rung, expected evidence, owner, and falsifying mutation or known-bad fixture. Unknowns are captured as exploratory rows with amendment triggers. Missing, silently dropped, or weakened rows block build and promotion.

title: Factory doctrine: Validator, Coder, Tester across three signed phases (2026-07-26)
content: Founder-supplied doctrine supersedes the prior Code/Test/Validate plus separate Testing Plan Proposal framing. Canonical roles are Validator, Coder, Tester. The signed spec is collaboratively produced across product specification (human proposes, Validator counters), architecture (Validator proposes, human debates and decides), and operational maturity (Validator proposes, human debates and decides). Coder and Tester receive the same spec but have no channel; neither sees or runs the other's artifact; Validator runs the tests and owns mutation evidence. Provenance of intent is the eighth non-negotiable. Canonical working copy: docs/SOFTWARE-FACTORY.md. Kindex node: 46922580e901.

title: factory_core intent provenance is canonical metadata, not semantic digest theater
content: factory_core/provenance.py makes each phase artifact carry canonical intent items and an externally trusted artifact digest. Downstream requirement, constraint, task, and test-assertion metadata carries artifact id, item id, and canonical intent digest. The verifier requires exactly one nonempty artifact for each phase, at least one claim, distinct human and Validator ratifiers, valid preserved-source digests, and resolvable exact references; promotion calls it directly and fails closed. ProvenanceBundle copies and freezes its trust map. It does not compare paraphrases or claim a hash proves meaning: semantic canonicalization happens in the human-plus-Validator phase loop. Local make ship closed green with 142 tests; this is self-verification, not independent Validator or live evidence. Kindex node: d1f3219db933.

title: Resolved factory role-channel contract: judge authority, no verdict negotiation, no Coder-to-Tester channel (2026-07-27)
content: Founder directed that the canonical working copy not retain the Coder-to-Validator contradiction as an open question. The resolved doctrine separates three controls: the Coder does not control the Validator's judgment, cannot negotiate a test verdict, and cannot communicate with the Tester. Defined question, failure, and specification-defect paths between Coder and Validator remain open. scripts/check_doctrine_sync.py now verifies the complete role-channel map and the resolved core-doctrine clause so the contradiction cannot silently recur.

title: Surface criticality composes with oracle adequacy and replaces consequence tiers (2026-07-27)
content: Founder-supplied criticality amendment replaces change-level consequence tiers/categories with human-decided Critical, Standard, or Cosmetic classes per surface. factory_core/criticality.py content-addresses the exact control profile and resolves explicit disturbances plus declared side-effect closure; unknown, unclassified, incompletely reasoned, or non-human-decided surfaces become Critical. factory_core/promotion.py disposes missing oracle/evidence links by class (Critical block/no waiver, Standard candidate-bound expiring human risk acceptance, Cosmetic report-and-promote), while malformed, mismatched, fabricated, or negative evidence blocks every class. Its content-addressed attestation binds the profile plus every decision input: disturbed roots, gates, implementer/verifier/approvers, oracle/live/determinism/flake/retry observations, specialist/quarantine/risk records, evaluation time, provenance-bundle digest, and cited evidence addresses. Any post-attestation rewrite is an integrity failure. Critical observations must be deterministic, live, zero-flake, zero-retry, specialist-reviewed, and retain the two-distinct-human floor. Side-effect closure enforces supplied topology but does not claim the topology is complete; phase-2 enumeration/parity controls own that proof. Canonical working copy: docs/SOFTWARE-FACTORY.md §3.5. Kindex node: 409093e3d25d.

title: Invariant artifacts, scoped tool policy, checklist gates, and test disposition (2026-07-27)
content: The Product Specification, Architecture Specification, and Testing and Monitoring Strategy are the only intent authorities. Every downstream citation binds the exact whole-artifact digest and canonical item digest, so any signed amendment invalidates old work. The run tool policy is signed and content-addressed but is an enforcement projection, not a fourth intent source: every rule cites phase 2 or 3, every inventory item has exactly one Allowed, Sign-off-required, or Verboten tier, scopes are opaque target data, unknown and Verboten calls deny, and Verboten rules require subject-bound resource-refusal probes. The policy and candidate must bind the same exact phase-artifact versions. Gate items count only with individual subject-bound evidence and recorded_at; missing items remain visible gaps, while negative or invalid evidence blocks. A formerly passing/currently failing test is updated only when exactly one signed current item explicitly supersedes its old authority; unchanged current behavior requires fixing code. When a new artifact digest retains the same item id and canonical intent digest, rebind the test citation without weakening its assertion. If current signed items both retain and supersede that behavior, route the contradiction to the human. Core modules: factory_core/{evidence,checklist,tool_policy,test_disposition,provenance,promotion}.py. make ship: 190 passed. The core verifies records but does not claim to remove platform capabilities, persist live checklist events, route lanes, or notify humans. Kindex node: 576b24df3d88.

title: Software Factory errata: controls, independence tiers, monitors, reproduction (2026-07-29)
content: A green guard that comes back red is a SUSPECTED OVER-CONSTRAINT: it stops and routes to a human, and is never reclassified as a forcing test, because a guard misread as forcing breaks working behavior and defends it with a green suite. The Validator's self-referentiality (it judges against a spec it co-authored) is named as a real limitation bounded only by the human signature, the behavior ledger, and verbatim-and-ratify. Independence is a five-tier scale derived from the recorded arrangement and recorded per run, with every agent's model, version, and directive version, because that is what makes requalification-on-change auditable; a claimed tier the arrangement cannot support is a false verdict, not a weak one. Structural (implementation-informed) test mode is permitted only against a signed interface contract; otherwise isolation, and the forgone branch depth becomes the Validator's mutation obligation. Production monitors are phase-3 outputs derived from the specification, never the diff: a diff-derived monitor is a change detector that cannot catch day-one wrongness, and a monitor whose backreference does not resolve is an unauthorized assertion about production. Critical surfaces carry human-authored monitors. An agent that evaluates an alert may not delete or weaken the monitor that produced it; silencing is a change to the oracle and goes through the specification-defect path, with state carried on the monitor. A defect is reproduced in a disposable environment and recorded before any repair is written; impossible reproduction is a declared lane condition that gates. Detection is exhaustive, notification is earned. Declined: monitor density as a target (recorded, never gated), ranking findings by category over incidence, and a single refutation rate across defect and absence claims. The hazard-merge ratification seat is filled from a named delegate roster rather than blocking on one accountable human.

title: Errata enforcement surfaces in factory_core and factory_runtime (2026-07-29)
content: factory_core/independence.py derives the independence tier from the recorded arrangement (mechanism ids -> strongest, shared context -> weakest, open channel -> weak, same model family -> moderate, different families -> stronger) with fail-closed defaults, so an unrecorded arrangement derives the weakest tier and an overclaim blocks. factory_core/monitors.py verifies the phase-3 monitor set: derivation, resolvable authority, class-scoped authorship against the enrolled roster, actionable-conclusion-before-notification, and recorded-only density. factory_core/triage.py denies delete/weaken/silence without a human-ratified specification defect bound to that monitor and action, ratified by someone other than the evaluator. factory_core/correction.py classifies each control by its DECLARED red-now/green-now role, so no observed result can promote a guard into a forcing test, and requires a reproduction recorded before the repair. All four wire into decide_promotion (lane, independence, monitors, correction) and into the promotion attestation subject; CriticalityProfile carries the Critical ratification delegate roster. The runtime evidence bundle now requires the declared lane, the independence record, and the monitor set: because the bundle IS the record, the closed schema refuses to write one that omits them, and AuthorityPolicy.segregation_policy() projects the signed genesis roster so human-authored monitors mean enrolled humans. scripts/check_doctrine_sync.py holds the prose side of each new rule with mutation tests proving the checks are sensitive.

title: Factory macOS isolation grants the trusted Python runtime read-only (2026-08-01)
content: GitHub's macos-14 isolation job failed before its denial probes because actions/setup-python installed CPython under /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework while the Seatbelt profile only named Homebrew and /usr/local runtime layouts. factory_runtime/isolation.py now derives and freezes read-only grants from sys.prefix, sys.base_prefix, and the resolved sys.executable parent before any lane starts, rejects a filesystem-root grant, and leaves lane write and network permissions unchanged. Those paths are explicitly part of the host trusted computing base, not lane-controlled input. Verification covered make ship, native Seatbelt denial and cross-lane proofs, a populated virtualenv pyvenv.cfg case, and real Tessera integration. Kindex node: 9a69c0751603.
